summary: Defines Trickle ICE, an extension of the ICE protocol for finding a working network path between two endpoints. Instead of gathering every possible address before starting, agents exchange candidates gradually and begin connectivity checks right away. This can speed up setting up a session considerably.

plainLanguage.summary: Trickle ICE lets endpoints exchange possible network addresses as they discover them. They can begin testing a path before they have collected every candidate.

subtitle: Connectivity checks can start while ICE candidates are still being gathered.

tldr.problem: Regular ICE waits for candidate gathering to finish before checking paths, and STUN or TURN work can delay session setup.
tldr.mechanism: Trickle ICE sends candidates as they become available and starts checks as soon as candidate pairs can be formed.
tldr.outcome: Gathering and connectivity checks can run in parallel. RFC 8863 later updated this specification.

today: RFC 8838 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2021. It has been updated by RFC 8863.

sections.title: Why ICE Uses Trickling
sections.content:
Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) gathers possible addresses, exchanges them with a peer, forms pairs, and tests connectivity. Gathering can involve STUN requests and TURN relay allocations, which can extend setup time.

Trickle ICE lets agents exchange candidates incrementally while gathering continues. As soon as an agent has a candidate pair, it can begin connectivity checks rather than waiting for a complete list.
sections.plainLanguage: ICE tests possible network paths between two endpoints. Trickle ICE allows the tests to begin while the endpoints are still finding paths.

sections.title: Determining Support
sections.content:
A using protocol should let endpoints discover Trickle ICE support before a session or require support from all endpoints. If an agent learns the peer does not support it, the agent MUST use regular ICE or abandon the session.

An ICE description may include the trickle option. It must apply at session level or to every data stream, not only some streams. The exact signaling format depends on the using protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The endpoints need to know whether both can trickle candidates. If one cannot, they use regular ICE or stop the session.

sections.title: Exchanging New Candidates
sections.content:
When an agent discovers a new local candidate, it checks whether that candidate is redundant. It then sends a new candidate to the peer through the using protocol. Candidates and end-of-candidates indications MUST arrive exactly once and in the same order they were sent.

Each trickled candidate must be tied to the correct ICE session, identified by the Username Fragment and Password combination. An agent MUST NOT form a pair from a local candidate until it has sent that candidate to the peer.
sections.plainLanguage: Each endpoint sends a new candidate after it finds one. The signaling system must deliver each candidate once, in order, and identify the ICE session it belongs to.

sections.title: Checklists That Can Grow
sections.content:
Trickle ICE checklists can begin empty because candidates arrive over time. An agent keeps an empty checklist Running while it expects more pairs; otherwise regular ICE could mark it Failed too early.

A newly formed pair starts in Waiting if it is the top pair for its foundation or if another pair for that foundation has succeeded. In other cases it starts Frozen. If a checklist reaches the default limit of 100 pairs, failed or lower-priority pairs should be removed to make room.
sections.plainLanguage: A checklist can be empty while an endpoint is still finding candidates. The agent waits for more candidates instead of treating the empty list as a failed connection.

sections.title: End of Candidates and Half Trickle
sections.content:
When candidate gathering ends, an agent sends an end-of-candidates indication for the current ICE session. After sending it, the agent MUST NOT send more candidates in that session, and the receiver ignores candidates that arrive later for that stream.

Half trickle sends a full generation of candidates in the initial description, so a regular ICE peer can process it. If the responder supports Trickle ICE, it can answer with fewer candidates and send the rest later.
sections.plainLanguage: When an endpoint has no more candidates, it tells the peer. Half trickle sends a full starting list so an older ICE endpoint can still respond.

sections.title: Privacy and Security
sections.content:
Trickle ICE inherits the security considerations of the ICE specification. Candidate signaling must be associated with the right ICE session so delayed information from an earlier session is not applied to a restart.

If revealing a host address is a privacy concern, an agent can omit candidates from its initial description and trickle only candidates that do not reveal host addresses, such as relayed candidates.
sections.plainLanguage: Network candidates can reveal an endpoint's addresses. An endpoint concerned about this can send only candidates that hide its host address.
